video_goal: Demonstrate how to prepare a piping bag and pipe buttercream rosettes and borders on a cake using a Wilton 1M tip.
required_subjects_and_props: Wilton 1M piping tip, clear plastic piping bag, scissors, buttercream frosting, silicone spatula, frosted cake, cake turntable, parchment paper

outline_steps.visual_action: Drop a metal Wilton 1M piping tip into an empty, clear plastic piping bag, pushing it down to the pointed end.
Use scissors to snip the tip of the plastic bag, allowing the open star shape of the 1M tip to push through and lock tightly into place.
Use a silicone spatula to scoop thick buttercream frosting and scrape it into the wide opening of the piping bag.
Twist the top of the piping bag tightly with one hand, forcing the buttercream down until it is visible inside the metal 1M tip.
Squeeze the bag to pipe a small, star-shaped test dollop of buttercream onto a scrap of parchment paper.
Hold the piping bag at a 90-degree angle, hovering the 1M tip half an inch above the top edge of a smooth, frosted cake resting on a turntable.
Apply steady pressure to the bag to pipe a small center star of buttercream directly onto the cake surface.
Without releasing pressure, move the tip in a tight, continuous circular motion around the center star to form a rosette.
Release the pressure on the bag completely, then gently pull the tip away in a horizontal sweeping motion to taper off the buttercream tail.
Use the non-dominant hand to rotate the cake turntable a few inches to the left, exposing a blank section of the cake edge.
Pipe a second buttercream rosette immediately adjacent to the first one, overlapping the tapered tail of the previous rosette.
Move the tip to the bottom base of the cake, squeezing and pulling horizontally in short bursts to create a continuous shell border.
Slowly spin the turntable 360 degrees to display the finished cake, highlighting the textured buttercream rosettes and shell border.
